theme_zh: 寫一份大家會看的每週進度報告

reading.title: Writing a Weekly Status Update That People Actually Read
paragraphs: Every Friday afternoon, thousands of project managers sit down to write a weekly status update, and many of their colleagues never read past the first line. That is a shame, because a good update does two jobs at once: it keeps stakeholders informed, and it shows that you are in control of your work.

The most useful updates follow a simple structure. Start with the big picture in one sentence: "The website redesign is on track for the December launch." Then explain what has happened so far. Mixing tenses here is natural. "We have finished the new homepage" tells people where the project stands now, while "The client approved the design on Tuesday" describes a specific event.

Next, be honest about problems. If the team has fallen behind, say so and explain why. A sentence like "We lost two days last week because the test server went down" is far more helpful than silence. Name any blockers, and say what you need to remove them: a decision, a document, or simply someone to sign off on the budget.

Finish with next steps and dates. "We will wrap up testing by Wednesday and follow up with the legal team on Thursday" leaves no doubt about what happens next. Readers also appreciate it when you mark each milestone clearly, so they can see progress week by week.

Finally, keep it short. If the update takes longer than five minutes to read, people will skip it. Bullet points, bold dates, and plain language will do more for your reputation than a long, perfectly written report that nobody opens.

questions.q: According to the article, what two things does a good status update do?
options: It keeps stakeholders informed and shows you are in control of your work.
It replaces meetings and saves the company money.
It lists every task you did and proves you were busy.
It gives your manager a reason to extend the deadline.
questions.explain_zh: 第一段：a good update does two jobs at once: it keeps stakeholders informed, and it shows that you are in control of your work。

questions.q: What does the writer recommend doing if the team has fallen behind?
options: Leave it out of the update until the problem is solved.
Say so clearly and explain why.
Blame the department that caused the delay.
Ask for a new deadline in the first sentence.
questions.explain_zh: 第三段：If the team has fallen behind, say so and explain why，要誠實說出來並說明原因。

questions.q: What can we infer about the writer's view of long, detailed status reports?
options: They are the best way to show how hard you work.
They are necessary for large projects.
They are less useful than short updates that people actually read.
They should only be sent to senior managers.
questions.explain_zh: 最後一段：短而清楚的報告 will do more for your reputation than a long, perfectly written report that nobody opens，可推論作者認為沒人看的長報告價值不高。這題考推論。

grammar.point_zh: 現在完成式 vs 過去簡單式
grammar.explain_zh: 現在完成式（have/has + 過去分詞）說的是「到目前為止」的進度或結果，不講明確時間，常搭配 already、yet、so far、this week。過去簡單式（V-ed 或不規則過去式）說的是在某個「已經結束的時間點」發生的事，常搭配 yesterday、last week、on Tuesday、in 2024。回報工作時，先用現在完成式講整體進度（We've finished the homepage），再用過去簡單式講具體事件（The client approved it on Monday）。只要句子裡有明確的過去時間，就不能用現在完成式。
grammar.pattern: have/has + p.p.（過去分詞）（+ already / yet / so far / this week）vs 過去式 V-ed／不規則過去式 + yesterday / last week / on Monday / in 2024

examples.en: We have finished the homepage, but we haven't started the checkout page yet.
examples.zh: 首頁已經完成了，但結帳頁還沒開始做。

examples.en: The client approved the design on Tuesday.
examples.zh: 客戶星期二批准了設計。

examples.en: I've sent three reminders this week, and he finally replied an hour ago.
examples.zh: 我這週已經寄了三次提醒，他一小時前終於回了。

exercises.q: We ___ (finish) the first draft, but we haven't sent it to the client yet.
exercises.explain_zh: 重點是「到目前為止」的進度，後半句的 haven't … yet 也是現在完成式，用 have finished。

exercises.q: The client ___ the budget last Friday.
options: has approved
approved
have approved
approves
exercises.explain_zh: last Friday 是明確的過去時間，要用過去簡單式 approved。

exercises.q: ___ you ___ the report to Daniel yet?
options: Has / sent
Have / sent
Have / send
Did / sent
exercises.explain_zh: yet 搭配現在完成式：Have you sent…? 過去分詞要用 sent。

exercises.q: I ___ (talk) to the vendor on Monday, and they promised a new delivery date.
exercises.explain_zh: on Monday 是明確的過去時間點，用過去簡單式 talked。

options: We have lost two days last week.
We lost two days last week.
We have lose two days last week.
We were lost two days last week.
exercises.explain_zh: last week 是明確的過去時間，不能用現在完成式；We lost two days last week 才正確。

lines.name: Grace

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Tom
lines.text: Great. What about the checkout page? That was the big one.

lines.name: Grace

lines.name: Tom

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Grace

prompts.question: Give a one-minute status update on a project you are working on (real or imagined). Say whether it is on track, what you have done so far, what happened last week, and what the next step is.
prompts.question_zh: 針對你手上的一個專案（真實或想像的都可以）做一分鐘的進度報告：整體是否正常、目前做到哪、上週發生了什麼、下一步是什麼。
hints: Headline: Overall, we're on track for… / We've fallen a bit behind on…
Progress so far: We've finished… / We haven't started… yet
Specific events: Last Tuesday, we… / On Friday, the client…
Next step: We'll wrap up… by… / I'll follow up with…
prompts.sample: Overall, the new training program is on track for the January launch. So far, we've written all six modules and recorded three of the videos. Last Wednesday, HR signed off on the content, which was a big milestone. The only blocker is the studio: it was double-booked last week, so we lost two recording days. I've already booked new dates, and we'll wrap up recording by the end of next week.

prompts.question: A friend you haven't seen for a while asks, "So, what have you been up to?" Talk about something you have done recently and one specific thing you did last weekend.
prompts.question_zh: 一個好一陣子沒見的朋友問你「最近在忙什麼？」請說說你最近做了什麼，以及上週末做了哪一件具體的事。
hints: Recently: I've been pretty busy with… / I've started…
Last weekend: On Saturday, I… / We went to…
Ask back: How about you? What have you been up to?
prompts.sample: Not much, honestly! Work has been busy, and I've started taking an online English course. I've already finished the first three lessons. Last weekend, I finally took a break. On Saturday, I went hiking with my sister, and on Sunday we tried a new ramen place near my apartment. How about you? What have you been up to?

writing.task: Write this week's status update email to your manager, Linda, about the new onboarding app. Include one sentence on the overall status, what the team has done so far, one problem with a specific date, and the next steps.
writing.task_zh: 寫一封本週進度報告 email 給主管 Linda，主題是新的員工到職 App：先用一句話說整體狀況，再寫團隊目前做到哪、一個發生在特定日期的問題，以及接下來的步驟。
writing.sample:
Hi Linda,

Here's this week's update on the onboarding app.

Overall: We're on track for the launch on December 1.

Progress: We've finished the login screen and the welcome tour, and HR signed off on the final wording on Tuesday. We've also started testing on Android.

Problems: We lost a day on Wednesday because the test devices arrived late. The main blocker right now is the privacy policy, which we still haven't received from Legal.

Next steps: We'll wrap up Android testing by next Friday, and I'll follow up with Legal on Monday.

Let me know if you have any questions.

Best,
Mimi

講「目前做到哪」用現在完成式（We've finished…）
講「特定日期發生的事」用過去簡單式（on Tuesday, HR signed off…）
誠實點出卡關的地方和需要誰幫忙

reading.title: Why Your Status Report Is Being Ignored (and How to Fix It)
paragraphs: Ask a group of executives what they think of the status reports that land in their inboxes every Friday, and you will hear the same complaints over and over: too long, too late, and too vague. Yet the people writing those reports are often working around the clock. The problem is rarely effort. It is that most updates are written for the writer, not the reader.

The first mistake is burying the lede. A manager who has thirty seconds to scan your update wants the headline up front: are we on track, slipping, or in trouble? Instead, many reports open with three paragraphs of background before getting to the point. By the time the bad news appears, half the audience has stopped reading.

The second mistake is sugarcoating. Nobody enjoys admitting that a deadline has slipped, so writers reach for soft phrases: "slightly behind," "minor delays," "a few open items." Experienced readers have learned to treat this language as a red flag. Paradoxically, a blunt sentence such as "We missed Tuesday's deadline and will need one more week" builds far more trust than a page of careful hedging.

The third mistake is getting lost in the weeds. A status update is not a diary. Listing every meeting you attended and every email you sent proves that you were busy, but it tells stakeholders nothing about where the project stands. Separate what has been achieved so far from what happened this week, and cut anything that does not change the picture.

Finally, a good update takes ownership. When something has gone wrong, say what you have already done about it and what you need from others. Readers do not expect a project to run without a hitch; they expect the person running it to be on top of the problems. Get that right, and your Friday email may become the one report people actually look forward to.

questions.q: According to the writer, what is the real reason most status reports disappoint their readers?
options: The writers do not put in enough effort.
They are written with the writer's needs in mind rather than the reader's.
Executives do not have time to read anything on Fridays.
Most projects are actually in trouble.
questions.explain_zh: 第一段：The problem is rarely effort. It is that most updates are written for the writer, not the reader。

questions.q: What does the writer mean by "burying the lede"?
options: Hiding bad news from senior management completely
Putting the most important information after a lot of background
Writing the update too late on Friday
Using too many technical terms
questions.explain_zh: 第二段說主管想先看到 headline，但很多報告 open with three paragraphs of background before getting to the point，可推論 burying the lede 是把重點埋在一堆背景之後。這題考推論。

questions.q: Why do experienced readers treat phrases like "minor delays" as a red flag?
options: They suspect the problem is bigger than the words suggest.
They think the writer is being too negative.
Such phrases are usually grammatically incorrect.
They prefer reports with no mention of problems.
questions.explain_zh: 第三段：寫的人為了不想承認延誤而用軟性說法，有經驗的讀者看到這種話就當成警訊，可推論他們懷疑實際問題比字面上嚴重。這題考推論。

questions.q: What can we infer about what stakeholders value most in a project manager?
options: A project that never has any problems
Being aware of problems and acting on them
Sending the longest and most detailed report
Avoiding any mention of deadlines
questions.explain_zh: 最後一段：Readers do not expect a project to run without a hitch; they expect the person running it to be on top of the problems，重點是掌握並處理問題，而不是零問題。這題考推論。

listening.title: Before the steering committee

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Marcus
lines.text: Priya, quick question before the steering committee. I read your update. It says "slightly behind." What does that actually mean?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Priya
lines.text: Right, so, um... We've slipped about a week on the data migration. We hit a problem with the legacy database on, I think, the 24th...

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Marcus
lines.text: A week. Okay. And you've known since the 24th?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Priya
lines.text: We've known it was a risk, yes. We only confirmed it was a full week on Friday, when the vendor got back to us.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Marcus
lines.text: So why didn't the update just say "one week late"? I'd much rather hear that than "slightly behind."

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Priya
lines.text: Fair enough. Honestly, I didn't want to sound alarmist before we had a recovery plan, but, yeah, I should've been more direct.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Marcus
lines.text: Okay, fine. Do we have a recovery plan now?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Priya
lines.text: We do. We've already brought in a second engineer, and we've moved the user training back a week, so the go-live date hasn't changed. The one thing I need is for Finance to sign off on the extra contractor days.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Marcus
lines.text: How many days are we talking? Ballpark.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Priya
lines.text: Roughly ten. I sent the request on Monday, and I've followed up twice, but I haven't heard anything.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Marcus
lines.text: Leave Finance to me. I'll grab Hannah after the meeting. And Priya? In the committee, lead with the headline. One week late, go-live unchanged, here's why.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Priya
lines.text: Got it. Headline first, then the details.

questions.q: How far behind is the data migration?
options: About two days
About a week
About a month
It is not behind at all.
questions.explain_zh: Priya：we've slipped about a week on the data migration。

questions.q: Why did Priya write "slightly behind" instead of "one week late"?
options: She did not know how long the delay was.
She did not want to sound alarmist before she had a recovery plan.
Marcus asked her to keep the update positive.
The vendor told her the delay was minor.
questions.explain_zh: Priya：I didn't want to sound alarmist before we had a recovery plan。

questions.q: What can we infer about how Marcus feels by the end of the conversation?
options: He wants to cancel the project.
He is unhappy with the vague wording but satisfied with the recovery plan.
He thinks Priya should be replaced as project manager.
He is pleased with the way the update was written.
questions.explain_zh: Marcus 一開始追問 slightly behind 到底是什麼意思，聽完補救計畫後說 Okay, fine，還主動幫忙去找 Finance，可推論他對措辭不滿、但對計畫本身是放心的。這題考推論。

questions.q: What does Marcus mean by "lead with the headline"?
options: Start the presentation with the most important point.
Write a title for the update.
Let the committee chair speak first.
Read the newspaper before the meeting.
questions.explain_zh: Marcus 接著示範：One week late, go-live unchanged, here's why，就是一開口先講最重要的結論。這題考推論。

dictation: We've slipped about a week on the data migration.
I sent the request on Monday, and I've followed up twice, but I haven't heard anything.
In the committee, lead with the headline.

glossary.zh: 把重點埋在後面（新聞寫作用語）
glossary.definition: to put the most important information after less important details

glossary.zh: 把壞消息說得好聽、粉飾
glossary.definition: to make something bad sound more pleasant than it really is
a sign that something is wrong or may become a problem

glossary.zh: 陷在細節裡、見樹不見林
